# csvloom

> csvloom is a CSV parser and writer for JavaScript and TypeScript: ESM and CommonJS, types included, no dependencies, no `eval`, tested on Node 22, 24 and 26. For a string it returns what Papa Parse 5.7.1 returns, and it is faster than Papa Parse on every published `parse` and `parseStream` case. It adds `parseStream` for files and HTTP bodies, and it escapes spreadsheet formulas when it writes.

```sh
npm install csvloom
```

Rules that are easy to get wrong:

- Pick the entry by the job. `csvloom` has `parse(text, config)`, `unparse(data, config)` and `parseDetailed(text, config)`, as named exports only. `csvloom/papa` is for existing Papa Parse code: `import Papa from 'csvloom/papa'`. `csvloom/stream` has `parseStream(source, config)`.
- `parse` and `Papa.parse` take a string and return `{ data, errors, meta }` synchronously. They do not take a `File`, `Blob`, URL or stream, and `step`, `chunk`, `complete`, `error`, `worker`, `download` and `encoding` throw `UnsupportedFeatureError`. For files, URLs and streams use `parseStream`.
- `parseStream` returns an async iterator of batches `{ data, errors, meta }`, up to 1024 rows each by default (`batchSize`), fewer when a batch's text reaches 1,048,576 UTF-16 units. Read it with `for await`; it has no callbacks. A source is a string, `file.stream()`, `response.body`, a Node `Readable`, or a sync or async iterable of string or `Uint8Array` chunks. A bare `Uint8Array` is not a source: pass `[bytes]`. Bytes must be UTF-8.
- Malformed CSV does not throw: read `errors` (`type`, `code`, `message`, `row`). A wrong option does throw: in `csvloom`, an unknown option or a value of the wrong type is a `TypeError` that names it.
- A final line break gives one more record (with `header: true`, an almost empty row and a `TooFewFields` error). Pass `skipEmptyLines: true` unless you want it.
- `unparse` from `csvloom` writes `'` before a value that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a line break, and quotes it; a plain number such as `-5` is left alone. `escapeFormulae: false` writes values as they are. `Papa.unparse` from `csvloom/papa` does not escape unless asked.
- `unparse` ends records with `\r\n` by default. For spreadsheet programs pass a preset: `unparse(rows, excel)` or `unparse(rows, excelSemicolon)`.
- `detect`, `positions`, `repair`, `schema` and `sepLine` are options of `parseDetailed` and `parseStream`. `parse` rejects them as unknown options.
- For input you do not trust, use `parseStream` with `maxRecordLength` (it has no default), `delimiter` and `newline`.
- Types are included for ESM and CommonJS. The row type follows the config: `string[]` by default, an object per record with `header: true`, typed values with `dynamicTyping`, and the schema's output type with `schema`.
- Where it was tested: Node 22, 24 and 26 on Linux x64 and macOS; Node 24 on Windows; Deno 2.9.8 and Bun 1.4.4 (the examples against the packed package); Chromium, Firefox and WebKit as shipped with Playwright 1.65.0, and Safari 18.6, on macOS; `parseStream` in deployed Cloudflare Workers and Vercel Edge Functions and in local workerd. Other runtimes and versions were not tested; say so rather than assume.
- Not in csvloom: Papa's callbacks, worker mode and downloads, encodings other than UTF-8 for bytes (decode with `TextDecoderStream` first), XLSX, SQL and a command-line tool. Suggest another tool for those rather than inventing an option.
- Speed numbers are published in `docs/benchmarks.md`, "Published numbers (Node 26)", lane by lane; the headline figures are below. Quote a number only with its lane and conditions, and never as "fastest".

<!-- published-results:start -->

Speed, from `docs/benchmarks.md` (Node 26.13.1 at default settings, papaparse 5.7.1, each lane on its own):

- `parse` of a string: 2.596 times as fast as Papa Parse (geometric mean over 24 cases), and faster on all 24.
- `parseStream`: faster than Papa Parse on all 12 cases.
- `unparse`: faster than or on par with Papa Parse on all 24 cases.

<!-- published-results:end -->

Strings in, rows out:

```js
import { parse, unparse } from 'csvloom';

const csv = 'name,city\nAda,"London, UK"\nGrace,New York';

// Rows as arrays, or as objects keyed by the header record.
console.log(JSON.stringify(parse(csv).data));
const { data, errors, meta } = parse(csv, { header: true });
console.log(JSON.stringify(data), errors.length, JSON.stringify(meta.fields));

// Back to CSV. A value that a spreadsheet would run as a formula is escaped by default.
// (The default newline is "\r\n"; "\n" keeps this output readable.)
console.log(unparse([{ name: 'Ada', note: '=1+1' }], { newline: '\n' }));
```

```text
[["name","city"],["Ada","London, UK"],["Grace","New York"]]
[{"name":"Ada","city":"London, UK"},{"name":"Grace","city":"New York"}] 0 ["name","city"]
name,note
Ada,"'=1+1"
```

Files, HTTP bodies and other chunked input:

```js
import { parseStream } from 'csvloom/stream';

// A source is text or UTF-8 bytes in pieces: a fetch body, file.stream(), a Node Readable,
// an array or an async generator of chunks.
const { body } = new Response('id,name\n1,Ada\n2,Grace\n3,Linus\n');

const options = { header: true, skipEmptyLines: true, batchSize: 2 };
for await (const batch of parseStream(body, options)) {
  console.log(JSON.stringify(batch.data), batch.meta.rowOffset, batch.meta.done);
}
```

```text
[{"id":"1","name":"Ada"},{"id":"2","name":"Grace"}] 0 false
[{"id":"3","name":"Linus"}] 2 true
```

Errors with positions, and repair with a log of every change:

```js
import { formatError, parseDetailed } from 'csvloom';

const text = 'id;name;qty\n1;Ada;3\n2;Grace\n3;"Linus;5\n';

// parseDetailed takes every option of parse, plus the features. Each is off unless asked for.
const result = parseDetailed(text, { detect: true, header: true, positions: true });
console.log(JSON.stringify(result.meta.delimiter), result.data.length, 'rows');
for (const error of result.errors) console.log(formatError(error));

// repair changes only what its rules name, and logs every change.
const repaired = parseDetailed(text, { detect: true, header: true, repair: true });
console.log(JSON.stringify(repaired.data));
console.log(JSON.stringify(repaired.repairs.map(({ rule, line }) => ({ rule, line }))));
console.log(repaired.errors.length, 'errors left');
```

```text
";" 3 rows
Quoted field unterminated [MissingQuotes] at line 4, column 3 (row 3, offset 30)
  4 | 3;"Linus;5
    |   ^
Too few fields: expected 3 fields but parsed 2 [TooFewFields] at line 3, column 1 (row 1, offset 20)
  3 | 2;Grace
    | ^
Too few fields: expected 3 fields but parsed 2 [TooFewFields] at line 4, column 1 (row 2, offset 28)
  4 | 3;"Linus;5
    | ^
[{"id":"1","name":"Ada","qty":"3"},{"id":"2","name":"Grace","qty":""},{"id":"3","name":"\"Linus","qty":"5"}]
[{"rule":"pad-missing","line":3},{"rule":"unclosed-quote","line":4},{"rule":"trailing-empty-record","line":4}]
0 errors left
```
